Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

effectzones 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial prototype.
  • geom_es_zones() draws effect-size magnitude zones; geom_mcid_zones() draws harm / trivial / benefit zones from an MCID. Both share one engine, leave the axis limits alone by default, support soft boundaries, either axis orientation, coord_flip(), facets and transformed scales.
  • Threshold objects: es_thresholds(), es_benchmarks(), mcid_thresholds(), mcid_distribution(); conversion with to_plot_scale() and pooled_sd().
  • plot_contrasts() for TukeyHSD, emmeans contrasts and data frames.
  • chen_or_thresholds() computes the Chen, Cohen & Chen (2010) odds-ratio equivalents of d for any baseline risk. Under their method protective and harmful zones are not mirror images, so the zones below 1 are computed from negative d (also in es_benchmarks("chen_or")).
  • es_thresholds() gains cuts_lower for asymmetric effect-size zones.
  • Both layers gain zone_labels to rename zones (all at once or by name).
  • The legend lists only the zones that appear in the plot.
  • plot_contrasts() accepts aov fits and emmeans grids of means directly, and recovers the model behind a TukeyHSD object (verified against the contrasts). The model’s residual SD is used automatically only for one-way models; otherwise sd must be given.
  • geom_mcid_zones(beyond = "multiples") now requires point MCID thresholds; with a range MCID the multiples would be uncertain too, so the combination is an error.
  • DOIs added for all cited references.
  • When plot_contrasts() cannot choose an SD for d (models with more than one term), the error now explains the rigorous procedure step by step, with a refit command tailored to the plotted term.
  • Package website: flatly theme, hex logo, and a new article, The mathematics behind effectzones, with step-by-step interactive calculators for every calculation the package performs.
